sections.html:
Eagle County is a mountain county in western Colorado with the Town of Eagle as its seat and Edwards as its largest community. The 2020 census counted 55,731 people, and the 2025 estimate is 54,291. Interstate 70 crosses the county east to west.

Much of the land is public. White River National Forest covers a large share and the Bureau of Land Management manages much of the rest, so check what your parcel borders before you list. Three school systems reach into the county: Eagle County School District RE-50J, Roaring Fork RE-1 and West Grand 1-JT, which is worth confirming for a buyer asking about a particular address.

sections.h2: How the Assessor values a home
sections.html:
The Eagle County Assessor values residential property by the market approach, using verified comparable sales as of a January 1 assessment date. The county reappraises in odd-numbered years, and the June 30, 2024 appraisal date applies to tax years 2025 and 2026. Sales data came from the 24 months ending June 30, 2024, or five years when data was thin.

Assessment rates have changed in the last few years:

  • 2024: 6.7% for residential, and 27.9% for vacant, commercial and industrial.
  • 2025: 7.05% for the school calculation and 6.25% for non-school, with other property at 27%.
  • 2026: 7.05% school and 6.8% non-school, with commercial improved and agricultural at 25% and all other at 26%.

For 2026 the non-school residential calculation also reduces actual value by 10% of the first $700,000. The school calculation uses the full value. If you own a second home and wonder whether that changes anything, ask the Assessor's office.

sections.h2: How the bill is calculated and why it rose
sections.html:
Assessed value times the combined mill levy gives the bill. About 90 taxing authorities set levies across roughly 367 taxing districts in the county. Bills for 2025 rose around 10% or more for many owners, because residential values climbed 8% under the reappraisal and a temporary $55,000 value reduction passed in 2024 expired.

The county average levy is about 65 mills, and some metro districts reach 125 mills, such as the Buckhorn area of Gypsum. The Tax Area code on your Notice of Valuation, in a format such as 236, P236 or SC236, tells you which authorities apply, and the county posts a spreadsheet of taxing authorities by area. Final amounts depend on the levies set in December, so confirm with the Treasurer in January.

Notices are mailed May 1, and appeals can be filed from May 1 through June 8, postmarked or delivered by that date. Ways to file:

  • Online at appealeaglecounty.com, which the county prefers.
  • In person from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. if you can't file online.
  • By mail to Eagle County Assessor, P.O. Box 449, Eagle, CO 81631, or by fax at 970-328-8667.
  • An agent needs your written authorization, and you should keep proof of mailing.

Useful evidence includes an appraisal dated within six months before June 30, 2024, sales details on your property or comparables, or corrections to property details. A follow-up inspection may be needed.

The Assessor mails a Notice of Determination on or before June 30. If you disagree, or hear nothing, file a written appeal with the County Board of Equalization by July 15. The office phone is 970-328-8640, or toll free 800-225-6136.

Pay in two halves, due the last day of February and June 15, or pay everything by April 30. Bills of $25 or less must be paid in full by April 30, and partial payments are not accepted. A payment postmarked on or before a deadline counts.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the lien sale
sections.html:
Real estate taxes still unpaid at the end of October are sold at the November tax lien sale, usually on the first or second Wednesday. The county's timeline:

  • May, June, August and September: calls or emails to delinquent owners when contact details are on file.
  • July 31: delinquent notice deadline. Payment by August 1 keeps a lien investor from adding current-year taxes to a prior lien.
  • October: unpaid real estate and mobile home taxes are published in the newspaper for three weeks.
  • November: the tax lien sale.

To redeem a sold lien, payment must reach the Treasurer by the last business day of the month, in cash or certified funds, from the owner of record. Seniors and active military can ask about deferral at colorado.propertytaxdeferral.com or (833) 634-2513.

sections.h2: Paying and getting a tax certificate
sections.html:
Call the Treasurer at 970-328-8860 for balances, and email taxcerts@eaglecounty.us to request a tax certificate. Payment options:

  • E-check online, for a $1.00 fee.
  • Card online.
  • Check payable to Eagle County Treasurer, mailed to PO Box 479, Eagle, CO 81631.
  • Wire. Call 970-328-8868 for instructions and verify them by phone, because the county warns of cyber fraud.

Bank bill pay can arrive late and unpostmarked, so interest may apply even when you paid on time. If a lender pays from escrow, the Treasurer cannot send duplicate statements to the mortgage company, since state law sends statements to the owner of record. Ask the office directly how a payoff works at closing.

sections.h2: What sellers in the Eagle valley run into
sections.html:
Common complications are large levies in some metro districts, reappraisal jumps and mortgage escrow shortfalls, and each can slow a conventional sale. Owners of inherited homes, out-of-area owners and landlords often want a clean exit with no showings. A cash purchase that accepts the house as it is, with tax and any lien paid from proceeds, fits that need.

Before you accept any offer, get the Treasurer's balance, confirm your Tax Area, and note whether a Board of Equalization appeal is still open, since a successful appeal lowers the next bill for whoever owns the house. At closing, the title company asks for the tax certificate, pays what is owed and records the deed.

A practical order for a seller: call the Treasurer for the balance, request the tax certificate by email, check which half has been paid, and confirm whether any late charge from the table above already applies. If a lien was sold at the November sale, remember that redemption needs cash or certified funds from the owner of record, so ask the title company to coordinate that payment rather than sending it yourself.

faqs.q: What is Eagle County's property valuation appeal window?
faqs.a: May 1 through June 8, postmarked or delivered by June 8. File online at appealeaglecounty.com or use the form on your Notice of Valuation.

faqs.q: When is the first half of Eagle County property tax due?
faqs.a: The last day of February. The second half is due June 15, and full payment is due April 30.

faqs.q: What is Eagle County's average mill levy?
faqs.a: About 65 mills on average, though some metro districts reach 125 mills.

faqs.q: Where do I send an Eagle County tax payment?
faqs.a: Eagle County Treasurer, PO Box 479, Eagle, CO 81631, with your tax coupon and account number.

faqs.q: What is the next step after the Assessor denies my appeal?
faqs.a: File a written appeal with the County Board of Equalization by July 15.
